articles.description:
Incident began at 2025-01-27 17:00 and ended at 2025-01-30 05:00 (times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)).

Mini Incident Report

We apologize for the inconvenience this service disruption/outage may have caused. We would like to provide some information about this incident below. Please note, this information is based on our best knowledge at the time of posting and is subject to change as our investigation continues. If you have experienced impact outside of what is listed below, please reach out to Google Workspace Support using the help article https://support.google.com/a/answer/1047213.

(All Times US/Pacific)

Incident Start: 27 Jan 2025 09:00

Incident End: 29 Jan 2025 21:00

Duration: 2 days, 12 hours

Affected Services and Features:

Google Drive, Gmail

Regions/Zones: Global

Description:

Users experienced an issue where PDF annotations were not displayed when using Google Drive Web and Gmail Web for a period of 2 days, 12 hours. All PDF data was still available if downloaded.

A preliminary analysis indicates the incident was caused by a code change that incorrectly determined which portions of a PDF to display.

Google engineers mitigated the issue by rolling back the affected client builds and deployed a preventative server fix to ensure this incident does not occur again.

Customer Impact:

Affected users were unable to see PDF annotations, such as filled form fields, shapes, freehand drawing, in the previewer.

Affected products: Gmail, Google Drive
articles.title:
RESOLVED: **Summary:**
Google Drive, Gmail Web, - Unable to see PDF annotations.
**Description:**
We are experiencing an issue with Google Drive, Gmail beginning at Wednesday, 2025-01-29 13:24 US/Pacific.
Our engineering team continues to investigate the issue.
We will provide an update by Wednesday, 2025-01-29 15:00 US/Pacific with current details.
We apologize to all who are affected by the disruption.
**Diagnosis:**
Customers using Drive Web, Gmail Web, opening PDFs would not see PDF Annotations (shapes, user added text, freehand drawing, etc). All PDF data is still available.
**Workaround:**
Open the PDF in a different tool.

Jan 30, 15:39 UTC
Resolved - On January 30th, 2025 from 14:22 UTC to 14:48 UTC, web requests to GitHub.com experienced failures (at peak the error rate was 44%), with the average successful request taking over 3 seconds to complete.
This outage was caused by a hardware failure in the caching layer that supports rate limiting. In addition, the impact was prolonged due to a lack of automated failover for the caching layer. A manual failover of the primary to trusted hardware was performed following recovery to ensure that the issue would not reoccur under similar circumstances.
As a result of this incident, we will be moving to a high availability cache configuration and adding resilience to cache failures at this layer to ensure requests are able to be handled should similar circumstances happen in the future.

Jan  9, 20:00 UTC
Resolved - On January 9, 2025, larger hosted runners configured with Azure private networking in East US 2 were degraded, causing delayed job starts for ~2,300 jobs between 16:00 and 20:00 UTC.  There was also an earlier period of impact from 2025-01-08 22:00 UTC to 2025-01-09 4:10 UTC with 488 jobs impacted.  The cause of both these delays was an incident in East US 2 impacting provisioning and network connectivity of Azure resources.  More details on that incident are visible at https://azure.status.microsoft/en-us/status/history (Tracking ID: PLP3-1W8). Because these runners are reliant on private networking with networks in the East US 2 region, there were no immediate mitigations available other than restoring network connectivity.  Going forward, we will continue evaluating options to provide better resilience to 3rd party regional outages that affect private networking customers.

articles.description:
Jan  3, 00:19 UTC
Resolved - On January 2, 2025 between 16:00:00 and 22:27:30 UTC, a bug in feature-flagged code that cleans up Pull Requests after they are closed or merged incorrectly cleared the merge commit SHA for ~139,000 pull requests. During the incident, Actions workflows triggered by the on: pull_request trigger for the closed type were not queued successfully because of these missing merge commit SHAs. Approximately 45,000 repositories experienced these missing workflow triggers in either of two possible scenarios: pull requests which were closed, but not merged; and pull requests which were merged. Impact was mitigated after rolling back the aforementioned feature flag. 
Merged pull requests that were affected have had their merge commit SHAs restored. Closed pull requests have…
articles.title: Incident with Actions

articles.description: Issue Summary:From 6:30 PM PST on January 28, 2025 to around 11:00 AM PST on January 30, 2025, some Slack AI customers may have experienced issues with Slack AI searches.A configuration issue with some of our Slack AI infrastructure resulted in an unexpected backlog of Slack AI tasks. This backlog meant that Slack AI responses were not served to users in a timely manner. Additionally, certain Slack AI queries had very long timeout windows, remaining in the queue indefinitely and contributing to the backlog. We scaled up our Slack AI infrastructure to increase our capacity to work through the backlog and manually ended any stuck queries. We also deployed a code change to set more reasonable timeout windows for the long-running queries, resolving the issue for all impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Slowness searching with Slack AI

articles.description: From January 25, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST, to January 27, 2025 at 8:00 AM PST, users on iOS 16 were unable to send messages in the Slack for iOS app after updating to version 25.01.40.We introduced some updates to the message composer in app version 25.01.40. However, these changes inadvertently caused a conflict with earlier workarounds intended to mitigate known issues with the iOS 16 keyboard. This caused the message composer to disappear when users tried to type messages.We implemented a fix to remove this conflict in app version 25.01.41, which resolved the issue for all impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Some iOS Users Unable to See Message Field and Send Messages

articles.description: Issue Summary:From 12:15 PM PST on January 15, 2025 to around 11:59 PM PST on January 24, 2025, some users may have experienced crashes in the Slack for Intune app on Android devices. In particular, the app may have crashed when accessing the Activity tab.We determined that a particular code change specific to version 25.01.30 of the Slack for Intune Android application was triggering crashes when users tried to view the Activity tab.We prepared a fix and packaged it for release as app version 25.01.31, then submitted this update to the Google Play Store. Once the update moved through the standard Google Play Store review process, the fix became available to all impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Intune App for Android crashing

articles.description: On Friday, January 24, 2025 from 12:28 PM PST to 2:01 PM PST, some users received error messages when running workflows with form submission steps.On investigation, we identified a routine code change had introduced an error condition into a subset of workflow steps related to form submissions, which caused workflows using those steps to fail.We rolled back this code change, which resolved the issue for all impacted users.

articles.description: On January 13, 2025 from 4:45 PM PST to 5:05 PM PST, users may have experienced brief issues with Slack, including connecting to Slack, sending and loading messages and threads, and running workflows.We made a planned changed to part of our infrastructure that inadvertently caused a problem on one of our database clusters, resulting in failures across a number of our API endpoints. Our automatic recovery systems stepped in and restarted the database cluster, restoring API success rates and resolving the issue for all impacted users.
articles.title: Outage: Issues connecting to Slack

articles.description: Beginning around November 22, 2024 until January 16, 2025, some users on the desktop versions of Slack experienced unexpected behavior with sidebar bolding & badging for direct messages (DMs), group DMs, and channels. This caused users to miss unread messages within these conversations.We initially were tracking reports from affected users, but on January 6, 2025, we noticed an unexpected increase of reports causing us to initiate our incident response processes.As an initial fix, we rolled out a change to the backend logic to correct the timestamp and store correct values so the client triggered the appropriate badging & bolding notifications. While this fix resolved the initial badging & bolding behavior, it unexpectedly caused an issue with badging counts, resulting in displaying an incorrect number of unread messages as well as not marking a channels read state correctly. We promptly reversed this change to avoid further impact.We continued our investigation efforts and discovered an additional cause within the backend logic checks related to how a message is routed to the client. This check ensures the client is fetching the proper information that triggers the notification badging & bolding. We adjusted the problematic logic within this check to ensure the proper data is fetched when triggering a notification, resolving the issue for affected users.Throughout this incident, we adjusted our strategy on how to best handle incoming reports from affected users, which impacted updates on our status site. As more users reported experiencing this issue, we then resumed our status site updates.We apologize for any confusion and disruptions to your work day and appreciate your patience as we worked to resolve this issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Some users may be experiencing issues with their sidebar not being badged for new DMs and channel notifications.

articles.description: From 6:00 AM PST to 11:30 AM PST on January 16, 2025, some users on Enterprise Key Management (EKM) enabled workspaces may have experienced intermittent errors while using Slack.An issue with part of our infrastructure caused a spike in errors on the EKM server cluster, resulting in inconsistent performance across Slack features including workflows, files, message posting, and huddles.We redistributed incoming traffic to unaffected server clusters, restoring normal service for all impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Some EKM users experiencing errors

articles.description: On January 6, from 3:23 AM PST to 4:50 PM PST scheduled workflows were not triggering correctly for some users.We identified that a recent update to our internal infrastructure had added unexpected load to the backend database that processes workflow triggers, which was causing scheduled workflows to fail.To mitigate further issues, we cleared these failed triggers from our systems. However, this inadvertently caused some workflows to re-trigger outside their scheduled time on customer’s workspaces.Once these failed triggers had been fully removed, we confirmed that scheduled workflows were working as expected again.
articles.title: Incident:  Scheduled workflows not triggering

articles.description: On January 6, 2025 from 12:14 AM PST to 11:09 AM PST, some customers were unable to switch between workspaces on desktop.We identified that an error had been introduced via a routine code change that prevented an upgrade prompt from closing as expected. As the upgrade modal retained focus while open, this prevented users with a workspace on the free plan from switching between workspaces.We reverted the code change and the issue was resolved for all impacted users.
articles.title: Incident: Some users cannot switch between workspaces

Resolved - The issue affecting the "Facebook Leads Ads - New Lead" module has been resolved. Leads are being fetched correctly. For customers impacted during the affected period (Monday, 27 January, 3:00 pm CET - Tuesday, 28 January, 12:30 pm CET), we will be sending out detailed email instructions on how to manually retrieve any missing leads using the "Watch Leads" module. We apologize for the inconvenience this may have caused.
Jan 28, 20:02 CET
Monitoring - We identified the root cause of the issue in our infrastructure and have taken steps to mitigate it. Leads were not reliably delivered in the period of Monday 27 January 3:00 pm CET - Tuesday 28 January 12:30 pm CET. According to our telemetry, fetching of new leads using the “Facebook Leads Ads - New Lead” module is now working correctly. Leads that were not delivered during the affected period will not be automatically redelivered and users will need to fetch the data from Facebook Leads Ads manually, using the Watch Leads module. Users who have contacted our Customer Support team have been informed about the workaround. We continue monitoring the situation.
Jan 27, 23:46 CET
Investigating - We experience issues with the "Facebook Leads Ads - New Lead" module, not fetching new lead correctly. Our dev team is investigating the issue together with Meta team. However, it seems to be caused by Meta API problems, as users across various platforms are reporting the same issue in their community.
As of now, we do not have an estimated time for resolution, and we regret any inconvenience this issue may cause.
articles.title: Facebook Lead Ads - "New Lead" module data
